title: Formal vs. Informal Register
description: Lær skilnaden mellom formelt og uformelt språk på engelsk, og vel rett register for ulike situasjonar.
competenceGoals: uttrykke seg med flyt og sammenheng med et variert ordforråd tilpasset formål, mottaker og situasjon

content.content:
## Register -- tilpass språket til situasjonen

Du snakkar annleis med vener enn med læraren din. På engelsk vert dette kalla **register** -- nivået av formalitet i språket.

Å velje rett register er viktig fordi feil register kan gi galt inntrykk: for formelt verkar stivt, for uformelt verkar uhøfleg eller uprofesjonelt.

I dette kapittelet lærer du:
- Kjenneteikn ved formelt og uformelt engelsk
- Ord og uttrykk i ulike register
- Korleis tilpasse register til mottakar og situasjon

content.title: Formal vs. Informal English
content.content:
**Formal English** (formelt engelsk):
- Vert brukt i: jobbsøknader, akademiske tekstar, offisielle brev, presentasjonar
- Kjenneteikn: lengre setningar, ingen samantrekkingar, presist ordforråd, passiv form
- Eksempel: "I would like to enquire about the available positions."

**Informal English** (uformelt engelsk):
- Vert brukt i: samtalar med vener, sosiale medium, chat, dagligtale
- Kjenneteikn: korte setningar, samantrekkingar, slang, forkortingar
- Eksempel: "Hey, are there any jobs going?"

**Semi-formal English:**
- Vert brukt i: e-post til lærarar, skuleoppgåver, nyheitsartiklar
- Midt imellom: høfleg men ikkje stivt
- Eksempel: "I'm writing to ask about job opportunities."

content.title: Eksempel: Same bodskap, ulikt register
content.problem: Sjå korleis den same bodskapen vert uttrykt i tre ulike register:
content.solution:
**Bodskap: Be om hjelp med lekser**

**Formal:** "I would be grateful if you could assist me with the homework assignment."
**Semi-formal:** "Could you help me with the homework, please?"
**Informal:** "Hey, can you help me with the homework? I'm stuck lol"

**Bodskap: Avslå ein invitasjon**

**Formal:** "I regret to inform you that I am unable to attend the event."
**Semi-formal:** "I'm sorry, but I won't be able to come to the event."
**Informal:** "Sorry, can't make it!"

**Bodskap: Takke nokon**

**Formal:** "I would like to express my sincere gratitude for your assistance."
**Semi-formal:** "Thank you very much for your help."
**Informal:** "Thanks a lot! You're the best!"

## Ordval: Formelt vs. uformelt

Mange ord har ein formell og ein uformell variant:

| Formelt | Uformelt |
|---|---|
| assist | help |
| enquire | ask |
| purchase | buy |
| commence | start, begin |
| reside | live |
| obtain | get |
| sufficient | enough |
| approximately | about, around |
| require | need |
| inform | tell |
| attempt | try |
| terminate | end, stop |
| request | ask for |
| utilise | use |
| numerous | many, lots of |

**Andre kjenneteikn:**

| Formelt | Uformelt |
|---|---|
| do not, cannot, will not | don't, can't, won't |
| One should consider... | You should think about... |
| It is recommended that... | You should... |
| Furthermore, Moreover | Also, Plus |
| However, Nevertheless | But, Still |
| Therefore, Consequently | So, That's why |

content.content:
## Email writing -- choosing the right register

Email is one of the most common forms of written communication, and choosing the right register is essential. Here are three models:

### Model 1: Formal email (to a company or official)

*Subject: Enquiry about summer internship opportunities*

*Dear Sir or Madam,*

*I am writing to enquire about possible summer internship opportunities at your company. I am a 15-year-old student at Sandvika School in Norway, and I am very interested in environmental science.*

*I would be grateful if you could send me information about any programmes available for young people during June and July.*

*Thank you for your time. I look forward to hearing from you.*

*Yours faithfully,*
*Emma Hansen*

**Kjenneteikn:** Full sentences, no contractions, polite phrases ('I would be grateful'), formal closing ('Yours faithfully' -- vert brukt når du ikkje veit namnet til mottakaren; 'Yours sincerely' -- når du veit namnet).

### Model 2: Semi-formal email (to a teacher)

*Subject: Absent from class tomorrow*

*Hi Ms. Johnson,*

*I'm writing to let you know that I won't be in class tomorrow because I have a dental appointment. Could I please get the homework so I don't fall behind?*

*Thanks,*
*Emma*

**Kjenneteikn:** Polite but relaxed, contractions OK ('I'm', 'won't'), first name basis is fine, shorter sentences.

### Model 3: Informal email/message (to a friend)

*hey lisa!*

*sooo I can't come tomorrow, got a dentist thing 😩 can u send me the homework? thanks ur the best!!*

*em x*

**Kjenneteikn:** Lowercase, emojis, abbreviations ('u', 'ur'), casual tone, no formal structure.

(1) E-post til ein arbeidsgivar: 'Yo, I wanna apply for the job. When can I start? Hit me up.'

I would appreciate information about the start date. Yours sincerely, [Name].' (2) For formelt for ein ven. Omskriven: 'Hey Alex, can't make it Saturday -- got something else on. Sorry!' (3) For uformelt for skuleoppgåve. Omskriven: 'Climate change is one of the most pressing issues of our time. Scientific evidence clearly demonstrates its significant impact on the environment.'

## Oppsummering

**Register** = formalitetsnivå i språket.

**Tre nivå:**
- **Formal:** Offisielle dokument, akademisk tekst, jobbsøknader
- **Semi-formal:** E-post til lærarar, skuleoppgåver, nyheiter
- **Informal:** Vener, chat, sosiale medium

**Formelt kjenneteikn:**
- Ingen samantrekkingar (do not, cannot)
- Presist ordforråd (enquire, obtain, require)
- Lengre setningar, passiv form

**Uformelt kjenneteikn:**
- Samantrekkingar (don't, can't)
- Enklare ordforråd (ask, get, need)
- Kortare setningar, slang, forkortingar

**Hugseregel:** Tenk alltid: Kven er mottakaren? Kva er situasjonen? Tilpass språket etter det.
